edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 2

source_text: Verum iam ipsa verba ponenda sunt, in quibus primum vox sponsae deprecantis auditur. Osculetur me ab osculis oris sui. Quorum iste sensus est: quousque mihi sponsus meus mittit oscula per Moysen, mittit oscula per prophetas? Iam ipsius cupio ora contingere, ipse veniat, ipse descendat. Orat igitur sponsi patrem et dicit ad eum: Osculetur me ab osculis oris sui. Et quia talis est, ut compleatur super ea propheticum illud, in quo dicitur: Adhuc loquente te dicam, ecce adsum, sponsam sponsi pater exaudit, mittit filium suum. Videns illa eum, cuius deprecabatur adventum, orare desistit et ad ipsum cominus loquitur: Quoniam bona ubera tua super vinum, et odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata.
pass_a_gloss: But already the-very words must-be-set, in which first voice of-bride praying is-heard: May-he-kiss me from kisses of-mouth of-him. Of-which this sense is: until-when to-me my bridegroom sends kisses through Moses, sends kisses through prophets? Already his-own I-desire mouths to-touch; he-himself let-come, he-himself let-descend. She-prays therefore to-father of-bridegroom... Father hears, sends his son. Seeing him she stops praying and near-at-hand says: Because good breasts yours above wine, and smell of-ointments yours above all aromatics.
notes: Pass A literalist gloss ≠ Pass B literary English.
Song lemma sense-checked against Baehrens; Lawson ACW not used for wording.
pass_b_english: But now the very words must be set down in which first the voice of the Bride at prayer is heard: [[Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:2]]. The sense is this: How long will my Bridegroom send me kisses through Moses, send me kisses through the prophets? I want already to touch his own mouth; let him come himself, let him come down himself. So she prays to the Bridegroom’s Father and says to him: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. And because she is such that that prophetic word is fulfilled over her — [[While you are still speaking I will say, Here I am >> Bible:Isaiah 58:9]] — the Bridegroom’s Father hears the Bride and sends his Son. Seeing him whose coming she had begged, she ceases to pray and speaks to him close at hand: [[For your breasts are better than wine >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:2]], and the fragrance of your ointments than all spices.
